All five decisions are in, pushed to **PR #24**, `verify` green.

## Confirmed and built

| | |
|---|---|
| **Rerolls** | 3/day pooled, not per-occasion |
| **Counter** | none — you find out when you hit it |
| **Closet** | 50 unarchived pieces free; the 10/day rate limit is gone |
| **Price** | €5/mo |
| **Packing mode** | stays in the tier + pitch, built later |
| **Share cards** | free, unchanged |

## Verified live, and the test was designed to catch a fake pass

I seeded three rerolls across **three different occasions** (work, evening, weekend), then asked for a Work reroll. Under the old per-occasion rule that would have been *allowed* — Work had only used one. It was blocked in 68ms with no model call and no new ledger row, so the pool is genuinely shared rather than the old code passing by luck.

The sheet reads: *"That's your 3 rerolls for today. Pro rerolls without limit."*

## Two stacking bugs — one mine, one already shipped

Your popup exposed that the bottom nav is `z-50` and renders after the page content, so anything at equal or lower z-index gets painted over.

**Mine:** the "Got it" button was hidden behind the nav.

**Pre-existing, and worse:** `RefineSheet` had the same defect *plus* it was an `absolute` child of `<main>`, so `overflow-hidden` clipped it too. Its **colour palette and its "Show 3 looks" button were both unreachable** — Refine has been partly broken since the generator shipped. Fixed both; screenshots confirm the palette and apply button now render.

## Docs updated so the record doesn't drift

`MONETISATION.md` §1 no longer says "never cap the closet" (it now distinguishes a ceiling on *quantity* from one on *capability*), §2 documents the pooled model and the no-counter decision with reasoning, the ceiling arithmetic is corrected to 7/day ≈ $0.63, and every price is €.

The design's `£5/mo` quote is left intact as a citation, with a note that **`profile-hub`'s "render verbatim" instruction is superseded for the price only** — the feature list still ships verbatim, so packing mode stays named.

I also recorded that packing mode is advertised before it exists, with the condition attached: acceptable while nobody can pay, must be built before Pro actually sells.

## Not verified live

The 50-piece cap. Your local closet is 22 unarchived, and filling it to 50 isn't practical. The logic is unit-tested including the archive-to-make-room path; the wiring point (`uploadAndTag`, before the storage writes and the Haiku call) is the same one I verified for the other gates.

CI passed, and the Node 20 warning is gone — the three remaining "deprecated" lines are unrelated noise (`punycode` from Node itself, and a transitive `node-domexception` dep). **PR #26** is green and ready to merge.

## Which plan we made

**Queue #7, `entitlements`** — merged as PR #25, `main` is `84e7766`.

It also **absorbed queue #8, `regenerate-quota`**: all four of its tasks shipped inside #7, so both plans moved to `done/`. I've marked #8 **do not execute** in the README, because running it now would actively break things — it specifies `profiles.plan` (we built `tier`), `is_regenerate boolean` (we built `kind text`), and a pool that counts drops. Its only unbuilt idea, showing the remaining allowance, is the one you rejected.

## What's next: queue #9, profile-hub → settings

It moved ahead of wear-stats for a concrete reason: **every gate we just shipped dead-ends.** The upgrade sheet's "Got it" has nowhere to send anyone, because the Pro card lives on the profile hub — and that card now has a real `profiles.tier` to read instead of a hardcoded state.

Two copy corrections are recorded against it before it's built:

1. **€5, not £5.** Its plan says "render that copy verbatim." That's superseded *for the price only* — £ is a design-file artefact, and the app already renders every price in euro. The feature list still ships verbatim.
2. **Packing mode stays named** in the pitch per your call, with the condition attached: it has to exist before Pro is actually sold.

After that, **#11 `styled-look-depth` is now unblocked** — it was waiting on #8 for metering, and its recorded schema defect is fixed since `generation_events.kind` has a `'styled'` value. Its Task 1 (running `diversify` on the styled shortlist) is independent and a cheap real quality win.

Written into `docs/STATE.md` as a working agreement, and into memory. Now the four things before I touch code.

## 1. The "outfits" stat is meaningless as specified — a defect in the plan

The plan counts all `outfits` rows. On your data that's **123**. But that table now holds every look ever generated, three per drop, plus styled looks and every past day's history. A profile boasting "123 outfits" is counting the generator's output, not anything you did.

Real candidates from your DB:

```
all outfits generated  123   ← what the plan specifies; means nothing
favourited               1   ← "Saved Outfits" isn't built yet
outfits worn             4   ← ties to the diary and the streak
```

I'd use **outfits worn (4)**. It's a fact about *you*, it's the same data the streak beside it uses, and it grows through the habit loop you're monetising. "123" would be inflated vanity that quietly gets worse every day the app runs.

## 2. Does the closet stat show the 50 cap?

This is the one I most want your call on, because it collides with a decision you just made. You said **no counter** for rerolls — a visible allowance makes people think about the limit constantly.

Does that principle extend here? `24` versus `24 / 50`.

They're arguably different: a reroll counter meters a *daily* allowance and creates recurring anxiety; a closet count is *inventory*, approached slowly, and someone photographing their wardrobe genuinely benefits from knowing where the ceiling is before they hit it at item 50. But it is still showing a limit, so I won't assume.

My lean: **plain `24`**, and surface the cap only when they're near it or hit it — consistent with "you find out when it matters."

## 3. The Pro card, and the dead end I shipped

Right now: gate → upgrade sheet → "Got it" → nothing. The plan makes the Pro card inert too, so profile → Pro card → nothing either. Every upgrade path terminates in a shrug.

There's no checkout and shouldn't be. But I could connect them cheaply: the sheet's button becomes **"See what's in Pro"** → `/profile`, and the Pro card lists all seven benefits rather than the one-line pitch. No fake purchase, but someone who hits a gate can actually find out what they'd get.

Also, since `profiles.tier` now exists, a Pro user must not see "Go Pro" — it should read as active. That one I'll just do; it's not a judgment call.

## 4. A flag for the settings plan (not now, but it affects data)

Settings specifies **"Auto-log worn looks: opening a look after 18:00 logs it."** I'd push back hard when we get there. Opening a look is not wearing it — and `wear_logs` is the foundation for cost-per-wear, streaks, most-worn, gathering-dust and gap analysis. Auto-logging on *view* would inflate all of it permanently, and there's no way to tell fabricated wears from real ones afterwards. Raising it now because it's a data-integrity decision, not a UI one.

---

Which way on 1, 2 and 3? Once you've called those I'll build the hub — profile-hub first as its own PR, settings after, per the small-scoped-plans preference.
1. Okay, do it. 2.i like ur approach. 3.Okay. 4. So what do u think we should to do?

## On 4 — my recommendation: never auto-write, ask instead

The core problem is that we have no evidence of wearing. Opening a look is the only signal available, and it's a bad proxy — you browse looks you reject. Auto-logging turns "I looked at this" into "I wore this", permanently, with no way to separate fabricated wears from real ones later.

That matters more than a normal data-quality issue, because **`wear_logs` is the thing Pro sells.** `MONETISATION.md` §1: *"Nobody pays for cost-per-wear on day one; they pay for it in month three, once the data is theirs."* If month three shows cost-per-wear computed from outfits they merely glanced at, the number is fiction and the whole compounding-value tier is worthless. We'd be poisoning our own paid feature to save one tap.

**What I'd do instead: an evening confirmation.** If you opened a look today and logged nothing, the app asks once — *"Did you wear Crisp Charcoal Contrast today?"* — Yes / No.

That keeps the entire convenience the toggle was for (you don't have to remember to tap "Wear this today"), costs one tap instead of zero, and every row in `wear_logs` stays true. It's also a *better* habit-loop moment than silence: a daily question is engagement, and the habit loop is what creates a payer.

It needs no push notifications — it triggers when the app is next opened in the evening, so it's buildable now rather than waiting on Phase 2.

Two consequences worth naming: it's **bigger than a toggle**, so I'd make it its own small plan rather than smuggling it into Settings; and Settings then ships with **rain guard as its only live toggle**, with this one absent rather than rendered dead — which is exactly the rule that plan sets for itself ("rendering a switch that schedules nothing is the lie this plan is trying to avoid").

content.text:
Yes — exactly that. Mechanically:

- **Trigger:** you open the app in the evening (say after 18:00 local), so no push notification needed.
- **Condition:** you opened a look today *and* logged nothing for today. If you already tapped "Wear this today", it stays quiet.
- **Ask:** *"Did you wear Crisp Charcoal Contrast today?"* — **Yes / No**, once per day.
- **Yes** writes exactly the same `wear_logs` row the button writes. **No** writes nothing and it doesn't ask again that day.

Two details that decide whether it helps or hurts:

**Yes and No must be equally easy.** If it's one "Yes" button with a dismiss ✕, people tap Yes to clear it and the data inflates anyway — the same disease as auto-logging, just slower. Two equal buttons keeps it honest.

**It only asks about looks you actually opened**, and if you opened several it asks about the most recent. We don't track dwell time, so "most recent" is the honest simple choice rather than guessing.

So it catches the forgetful case, which is the real one, without ever inventing a wear. I'll spec it properly when Settings comes up.

input.new_string:
## ⚠️ The mockup is the baseline, not a ceiling

**Standing rule, stated by the user 2026-08-05, and it cuts both ways.**
`design_handoff_stylist_generator/Fitcheck.dc.html` is the starting point for anything visual —
**but it is a prototype, not a specification, and we can do better than it.** The user's words:
*"not fully follow prototype, maybe we can do better on our own."*

The distinction that matters is **considered vs. accidental**:

- **Never silently drop what the mockup specifies.** That is the failure that prompted this. The Pro
  banner (`:694-698`) is a compact card — serif italic title, one-line pitch, and a **price pill inside
  the card**. I replaced it with all seven benefits printed into the card: uglier, *and* it quietly
  lost the price pill. Nobody decided that; I just didn't look.
- **Improving on it deliberately is encouraged.** Several already shipped and are better than the
  prototype: the occasion row (measured — a scrolling row hid 25% of the feature at phone width), the
  item-detail stat tiles (one type size, user call), the diary's day numbers (all in one corner, user
  call), and the Pro sheet itself — the mockup has no such screen, and a compact banner that opens a
  designed sheet beats either a bare banner or a wall of bullets.

**The bar:** open the mockup section first, list what it specifies, and account for every element you
are not reproducing — then improve on it on purpose, and write down why. A divergence you can defend is
fine. A divergence you didn't notice is the bug.

content.text:
**PR #27 open** — https://github.com/1curafu/Fitcheck/pull/27. 483 tests, tsc and build clean.

## What you caught, and what it turned out to be

The broken sheet wasn't a styling mistake — it was the **same bug as the diary's day number**. Newly-added arbitrary-value utilities (`size-[32px]`, `text-[12px]/[1.3]`, `max-w-[440px]`) silently don't resolve in this setup, so the icon tiles collapsed to zero width and the descriptions kept an inherited font size. That's why it looked like the text was sitting on top of the icons. Geometry is inline now, which is the fix that held last time.

Three things you were right about, in order:

1. **The bullet wall was terrible** — and worse, it silently dropped the price pill the mockup already had. The banner is back to the design's structure.
2. **The button belonged on the card.** Restored, `Go Pro · €5/mo`, inside the rust gradient.
3. **"Not now" was crowded.** Given its own spacing so it reads as a real second option rather than part of the primary.

The sheet now uses the design system's own spec-table pattern — hairline-divided rows with icon tiles — instead of a bare list.

input.new_string:
### ⚠️ Settings (#9b): do NOT ship "Auto-log worn looks" as written

The plan specifies *"when on, opening a look after 18:00 local logs it."* **Rejected — opening a look is
not wearing it.** `wear_logs` is the foundation of cost-per-wear, streaks, most-worn, gathering-dust and
gap analysis, i.e. of everything Pro sells. Logging views as wears inflates all of it permanently, with
no way afterwards to tell a fabricated wear from a real one — poisoning the paid feature to save one tap.
`MONETISATION.md` §1: *"they pay for it in month three, once the data is theirs."*

**Build an evening confirmation instead** (agreed with the user 2026-08-05): if you opened a look today
and logged nothing, ask once — *"Did you wear <look> today?"* — **Yes / No**. Yes writes the same row the
button writes; No writes nothing and it does not ask again that day. Triggers when the app is next opened
after ~18:00 local, so it needs no web-push and is buildable now.

Two details that decide whether it helps or hurts: **Yes and No must be equally easy** (a lone "Yes" with
a dismiss ✕ gets tapped to clear it, and the data inflates anyway), and it asks only about looks actually
opened, most recent first — dwell time is not tracked, so "most recent" is the honest simple choice.

It is **bigger than a toggle**, so it wants its own small plan. Settings then ships **rain guard as its
only live toggle** — which is that plan's own stated rule: *"rendering a switch that schedules nothing is
the lie this plan is trying to avoid."*

**Price/copy decisions already applied in #27** (kept here for the record): the price is **€5**, not the
design's £5 — the app targets the EU and every other price renders in euro. The feature list still ships
verbatim, **packing mode included**, which is deliberate while nothing can be bought; it must be built
before Pro is actually sold, or dropped from the copy then.
